# evaluateRules golden data

Regression fixture for `evaluateRules` (REFACTORING_PLAN.md Phase 0).

| File | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `notes.json` | 160 notes: 10 ages × 16 variants. Ids are `<age>-<variant>`; `30d` is exactly 30 days old (boundary, not deleted by the 30-day rule), `30d1s` is one second older. |
| `pinned.json` | ids of the `*-pinned` notes (what `i` → `pinnedNoteIds` would return). |
| `rules.json` | three rules, deliberately **unsorted** (180, 30, 60) to exercise sorting. |
| `expected.json` | `now` used for the evaluation and the expected list of note ids to delete, in evaluation order. |

## Provenance

Generated by `generate_golden.py` from the Python `days_expire.step3` at tag
`python-final` (the frozen Python version with the `reactionCount` fix). The
script also runs the unpatched `step3` (`python-final~1`) and asserts that the
two results differ **only** in notes whose id contains `reactionCount`; those
expected values were checked by hand against the rule semantics in
REFACTORING_PLAN.md §2.4 (a note is kept when `note.reactionCount >= rule.reactionCount`).

Notes with the `export-only` variant have no count fields, like a Misskey note
export, and are therefore only protected by `pinned` / `renote` / `reply` /
`inChannel` (§2.5).

The script is kept for traceability only; it needs the Python files that will
be deleted in Phase 4, so it will stop working then and the JSON files are the
source of truth from that point on.
